items.title: Cellectis could cut 70% of workforce in shift to in vivo therapies
items.snippet: Cellectis’ business transformation could cost around 160 global employees their jobs. The company has stopped enrollment in its two CAR T programs as it focuses on trials of its in vivo candidates.

items.title: PharmaLogic buys Lantheus plant to build transatlantic radiopharmaceutical CDMO
items.snippet: Less than two years after acquiring the assets, Lantheus is selling its CDMO unit and a New Jersey production plant to PharmaLogic.

items.title: Milestone cutting 20% of HQ team, including CMO
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Arrowhead’s Ionis problem, Kyverna’s next-gen end and more biotech earnings
items.snippet: When Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ Tryngolza undersold, investors immediately looked to Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals’ executives for answers on how they will navigate a launch in the same market.

items.title: HHS pumps up to $25M into ibogaine, other psychotropic drugs on Veteran’s Day
items.snippet: Ibogaine, which operates via a “matrix pharmacology,” has long been a focus of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Trump administration.

items.title: Windward nets $175M IPO, bringing 2026 biotech debuts to 35
items.snippet: Windward Bio’s public debut brings this year’s IPO count well above the sluggish total of eight in 2025.

items.title: Regeneron’s POTS antibody curbs heart rate spikes, teeing up Phase 3 trial
items.snippet: Regeneron’s mid-stage success in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome has the company gearing up to launch a Phase 3 study in the first half of 2027.

items.title: Biopharma pushes beyond GLP-1s, weight loss at ObesityWeek 2026
items.snippet: ObesityWeek 2026, which kicks off on Saturday, will spotlight presentations on the ascendant amylin pathway, as well as therapies looking to improve the quality of weight loss and patients’ persistence on treatment.

items.title: Webinar: Optimizing Cell Therapy Manufacturing Efficiency with Cryopreserved Cells
items.snippet: In this webinar, we will show how delayed isolation and cryopreservation of immune cells from fresh leukopaks can drastically impact their stability and functionality. We will also explore how purified and cryopreserved cell populations such as PBMCs and isolated T cells streamline logistics, reduce variability, and e...

items.title: Deep dive: Cardiovascular calamities and catalysts
items.snippet: BioSpace reviews upcoming cardiovascular milestones after a summer of missed targets.

items.title: Neurosterix nabs $105M, recruits Karuna veterans for schizophrenia push
items.snippet: Addex Therapeutics spinout Neurosterix will use the series B funds to advance an oral drug targeting M4, a muscarinic receptor also targeted by BMS’ Cobenfy, which introduced a new mechanism for treating schizophrenia with its 2024 approval.

items.title: FDA’s commissioner voucher program reportedly shuttered ahead of Senate vote on Overton
items.snippet: In advance of a Senate vote on Heidi Overton as the next FDA commissioner, the agency has shelved the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program introduced by former leader Marty Makary, Reuters reported Thursday.

items.title: Pfizer snags $1.5B financing from PE firm Blackstone to support Metsera asset
items.snippet: With 10 active or planned Phase 3 trials underway for Metsera’s berobenatide, Pfizer has signed a deal with Blackstone Life Sciences to finance the program to approval.

items.title: BMS R&D head to depart amid restructure
items.snippet: Bristol Myers Squibb is combining all research and development efforts under one leader as pressure rises to replenish its pipeline.

items.title: Can we finally get ahead of drug shortages?
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you'll hear from Christina Smolke, co-founder & CEO at Antheia and Kyle Pudenz, senior vice president and head of data & AI product at Cencora. We explore why drug shortages are getting worse, and how combining predictive supply-chain analytics with agile, distributed manufacturing could...

items.title: Biopharma layoffs rise YOY in October but sharply trend down for 2026
items.snippet: October marked the first time this year there was an increase in both the number of biotech and pharma companies trimming their workforces and the number of affected employees when compared to 2025. Still, it’s highly unlikely 2026 layoffs will come close to matching the downsizing seen last year.

items.title: 2026 Q3 Job Market Report: Job opportunities, layoffs show YOY improvement
items.snippet: During Q3, there was a 31% year-over-year increase in job postings live on BioSpace. The number of employees affected by layoffs dropped 90%.

items.title: 10 companies hiring in New Jersey
items.snippet: Looking for a biopharma job in New Jersey? Jobs on BioSpace increased year over year in October, and there are hundreds of open positions posted now.

items.title: FDA warns Chinese providers of compounding APIs over record-request refusals
items.snippet: Neither Chongqing Qiancan Technology nor Tianjin Healthcare Medical Technology provided the records requested by the FDA, leading the agency to issue import alerts and warning letters.

items.title: PepGen shares almost double as DM1 oligonucleotide achieves ‘best in class’ splicing
items.snippet: Mean splicing correction for PepGen’s PGN-EDODM1 was 46.5% at week 13, compared to under 30% for competitors like Dyne Therapeutics, Novartis and Ionis Pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
